paper_title: Mapping Polymer Donors toward High-Efficiency Fullerene Free Organic Solar Cells
source_file: /home/wzfeng/MySearch/PhotoRag/MD/Advanced Materials - 2016 - Lin - Mapping Polymer Donors toward High‐Efficiency Fullerene Free Organic Solar Cells/auto/Advanced Materials - 2016 - Lin - Mapping Polymer Donors toward High‐Efficiency Fullerene Free Organic Solar Cells.md

knowledge_points.content: Three key criteria for selecting polymer donors for non-fullerene organic solar cells include: appropriate energy levels for exciton dissociation and high Voc, complementary absorption with the acceptor to maximize Jsc, and morphological compatibility for ideal phase separation and charge transport.
knowledge_points.evidence: Establishing general design guidance of donor materials in nonfullerene OsCs is more important but more complicated than that in fullerene OsCs... we propose the following criteria as being important: i) The energy levels... ii) The donor should have complementary absorption... iii) The donor should have morphology compatibility.

knowledge_points.content: The organic solar cell based on the PTFBDT-BZS donor and IDIC acceptor, optimized with 0.25% 1,8-diiodooctane (DIO), achieved a peak power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 11.03% and an average PCE of 10.97%.
knowledge_points.evidence: PTFBDT-BZS:IDIC based devices with 0.25% DIO show even higher PCE up to 11.03% (the average value of 10.97% for 20 devices)

knowledge_points.content: Wide-bandgap polymer donors (PDCBT, J51, PTFBDT-BZS, and PDBT-T1) exhibit higher device performance when paired with the narrow-bandgap acceptor IDIC compared to the narrow-bandgap donor PTB7-Th due to better complementary absorption in the visible-NIR range.
knowledge_points.evidence: Among these systems, wide-bandgap polymers (PDCBT, J51, PTFBDT-BZS, and PDBT-T1):IDIC-based as cast devices show PCEs of 6.28%, 6.94%, 8.06%, and 9.20% respectively... which are higher than that of narrowbandgap polymer (PTB7-Th):IDIC-based devices (5.24%)

knowledge_points.content: The open-circuit voltage (Voc) of IDIC-based solar cells is directly related to the HOMO levels of the polymer donors; PTFBDT-BZS, which has the deepest HOMO level among the tested donors, yielded the highest Voc of 0.921 V.
knowledge_points.evidence: The Voc of these devices is in the range of 0.8–0.92 V, which is related to the HOMO of the donors... PTFBDT-BZS with the deepest HOMO yields the highest Voc

knowledge_points.content: The addition of 0.25% 1,8-diiodooctane (DIO) as a solvent additive in PDBT-T1:IDIC and PTFBDT-BZS:IDIC blends improves molecular packing, increases domain purity, and optimizes phase separation, leading to enhanced fill factor (FF) and short-circuit current (Jsc).
knowledge_points.evidence: use of 0.25% DIO boosts the PCE of OSCs based on PDBT-T1:IDIC and PTFBDT-BZS:IDIC up to 10.37% and 11.03%... DIO solvent improves the crystallinity, enhances phase purity, and optimizes phase separation of blended films.

knowledge_points.content: Resonant soft X-ray scattering (R-SoXS) analysis reveals that the relative domain purity of PTFBDT-BZS:IDIC blended films increases from 0.74 to 1.0 upon the addition of 0.25% DIO.
knowledge_points.evidence: The relative domain purity of PTFBDT-BZS:IDIC blended films without and with DIO is 0.74 and 1, respectively.

knowledge_points.content: In the PTFBDT-BZS:IDIC system, the relationship between short-circuit current (Jsc) and light intensity (P) follows Jsc ∝ P^1.0, indicating that virtually all free carriers are collected at the electrodes before bimolecular recombination occurs.
knowledge_points.evidence: Both PDBT-T1:IDIC and PTFBDT-BZS:IDIC without and with DIO show the relationship of Jsc ∝ P^1.0 which indicates almost all free carriers are swept out and collected at the electrodes prior to bimolecular recombination.

knowledge_points.content: Grazing-incidence wide-angle X-ray diffraction (GIWAXS) measurements indicate that PDBT-T1:IDIC and PTFBDT-BZS:IDIC blended films possess a predominant 'face-on' molecular orientation, which is beneficial for vertical charge transport between electrodes.
knowledge_points.evidence: The π-π stacking of these four blended films in the out-of-plane direction is stronger than that in the in-plane direction, which indicates a predominant 'face-on' molecular orientation... The vertical π-π stacking is favorable to charge transport

knowledge_points.content: Transient absorption (TA) spectroscopy shows that in PTFBDT-BZS:IDIC blends, approximately 50% of charge pairs are formed within 200 fs (prompt generation), with the remaining generation completed by approximately 30 ps (delayed generation) via exciton diffusion.
knowledge_points.evidence: Approximately half of charge pairs are formed within 200 fs, with a slower phase of charge commensurate with the 1.0 ps timescale of exciton quenching and complete by ≈ 30 ps.

knowledge_points.content: The coherence length (CL) of π-π stacking for the PTFBDT-BZS donor increases from 2.4 nm in as-cast films to 2.9 nm when processed with 0.25% DIO, while the IDIC acceptor π-π stacking CL remains at 4.9 nm.
knowledge_points.evidence: The coherence length of PTFBDT-BZS and IDIC π-π stacking is 2.4, 2.9 nm and 4.9, 4.9 nm for the blended films without and with DIO, respectively.

knowledge_points.content: Electroluminescence (EL) measurements of PTFBDT-BZS:IDIC blends show that the addition of DIO causes a redshift in the charge transfer (CT) state peak, which corresponds to a decrease in the open-circuit voltage (Voc).
knowledge_points.evidence: From the EL measurement... the addition of 0.25% DIO shifts the CT peak to lower energy. This redshift indicates lower CT energy in the blend processed with DIO and hence smaller Voc

knowledge_points.content: The optimized PDBT-T1:IDIC blend with 0.25% DIO achieved a high fill factor (FF) of 0.732, contributing to its peak efficiency of 10.37%.
knowledge_points.evidence: Table 1: PDBT-T1 with 0.25% DIO; Voc 0.834, Jsc 16.98, FF 0.732, PCE 10.37.
